title: Polynomial-size nondeterministic circuit recognition
statement: A language $L$ of Boolean strings belongs to the class described here if there are natural numbers $a,k$, a function $m:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and a Boolean circuit $C_n$ for each input length $n$, with $n+m(n)$ input bits, such that each circuit has fan-in at most two and size at most $a(n+1)^k$. For every Boolean string $x$, membership $x\in L$ is equivalent to the existence of a witness of length $m(|x|)$ for which $C_{|x|}$ outputs true on the concatenation of $x$ and that witness.
hypotheses_covered: $L$ is a language of Boolean lists
There is a circuit $C_n$ with $n+m(n)$ input bits for each $n$
Each circuit has size at most $a(n+1)^k$
Membership is equivalent to the existence of an accepting witness of length $m(|x|)$
